patUsageGuide.title: How to use Personal Access Tokens
patUsageGuide.intro: Personal Access Tokens (PATs) let you authenticate with the CybeDefend API without going through the browser login flow. They are ideal for CI/CD pipelines, scripts, and automation.
patUsageGuide.step1Description: First, fetch the available client application IDs. Use the one matching your integration (cli, vscode, or intellij):
patUsageGuide.step2Title: 2. Exchange your PAT for an access token
patUsageGuide.step2Description: PATs cannot be used directly as Bearer tokens. Use the client ID from step 1 to exchange your PAT via the OIDC token exchange endpoint:
patUsageGuide.step3Description: Use the returned access token as a standard Bearer token in your API calls:
patUsageGuide.note1: The PAT value (pat_...) can be displayed and copied from the token list. Store it securely.
patUsageGuide.note2: If a PAT expires or is deleted, any exchange using it will fail immediately.
patUsageGuide.note3: Each exchange returns a short-lived access token. Request a new one when it expires.

community.stepTitle: Use the token as a Bearer token
community.stepDescription: Send the token as it is in the Authorization header of your API calls. There is no exchange step:
community.note1: The token (cdp_…) is shown only once, right after its creation. Store it in a secret manager.
community.note2: A revoked or expired token is refused at once.
community.note3: A token cannot create, list or revoke tokens, nor change a password: that takes a signed-in session.
